message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole for locking my roommate and her friend out of our dorm room. Let me start by understanding the situation better. We have a dorm room with two beds and desks, pretty standard. My roommate and her friend have started doing this thing that's really annoying. Whenever my boyfriend and I are in our room, and they leave, they leave the door wide open. They laugh and say "this is what you get" as if it's some kind of punishment for showing minimal PDAs with my boyfriend in the room. But we're not doing anything, usually just watching Netflix in my bed. I feel like this is an invasion of my privacy. People in the dorm walk the halls, and I'm uncomfortable with that, especially since they're doing it intentionally to make me feel that way. Tonight, they left the room giggling and said "good luck" as they left the door open. They do this going in and out of the room like five times an hour. Each time I get up and close the door... I get sick of it on their like sixth trip, so I just lock the door. I know she has the key, but if I have to go through the hassle of getting up to close the door, they can go through the hassle of unlocking it. Anyway, the friend comes for their seventh trip and can't open the door and starts banging like crazy. I don't open the door because she knew what she was doing. She went back wherever she and my roommate were hanging and got the key and came in. Then she told me it was very rude that I locked the door because "it's my roommate's room." I calmly said if you're going to make me get up and close the door, you can go through the process of unlocking it. My boyfriend also asked why they were acting so passive-aggressive for no reason. She laughed and called me disrespectful again and left, leaving the door wide open. Am I really the asshole for just wanting my door kept closed so everyone passing by doesn't see me in my bed? I mean, I feel like I'm just trying to maintain some privacy, but they're making it really difficult. Is there a better way to handle this situation? Maybe I should talk to my roommate about it instead of locking them out. Or perhaps there's a compromise we can reach where the door stays closed but they still feel comfortable coming in and out. I don't want to escalate things further, but I also don't want to compromise my privacy. I wonder if other people have dealt with similar situations. Maybe there are some tips or strategies for handling roommate conflicts like this. It's tough because I don't want to be the bad guy, but I also don't want to feel like my privacy is being invaded constantly. Maybe setting some boundaries or having a conversation about expectations could help. I just need to figure out the best way to approach this so that everyone feels respected and comfortable in the shared space.
